comparator.name: Human Geography and Planning
comparator.sourceNotes: The degree includes 60 EC of first-year courses, a 30 EC track, 15 EC of major electives, 45 EC of profiling electives, and 30 EC of final-year research courses and thesis work.

components.name: Foundations of Human Geography and Planning
Borders in Perspective
components.note: Participate in Cities in Transition and Competing Claims on Space, and pass at least one of them before taking this course.

components.name: Theories and Approaches to Migration and Global Development
components.note: Start the track after earning at least 45 EC, passing Globalization and Development and participating in Spatial Data and Geographic Information and Socio-Spatial Research. Take the four track courses in one academic year.

components.name: Global Migration and Development: Key Themes
components.note: Participate in the track theory course before taking this course.

components.name: Mixed Methods Research Project
components.note: Participate in the track themes course and pass Spatial Data and Geographic Information before starting the project.

components.name: Trans-Mob Lab
components.note: Participate in both the theory and themes courses and pass at least one of them before starting the lab.

components.name: Profiling Electives
components.note: Choose 45 EC of electives, with at least 15 EC at intermediate level or above. Options include an eligible minor, study abroad or a placement.

components.name: Analysis
components.note: Pass the Mixed Methods Research Project before taking Analysis.

components.name: Research Design
components.note: Pass the eight first-year courses and complete the track before taking Research Design.

components.name: Bachelor’s Thesis
components.note: Pass the eight first-year courses, all four track courses and Research Design, and participate in Science and Society and Analysis before starting the thesis.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest programme integrates the target’s social-spatial, environmental and mixed-method core. The first two evidenced track directions after that core—migration/global development and inclusive cities—produce feasible, materially different UCR curricula. Planning sustainable cities and innovative sustainable regions are also coherent but production stops at the three-alternative maximum.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both use delta environments to study water management, environmental risk and adaptation.
Utrecht studies how planning decisions mediate competing claims on land.
Both use geographic data and maps to investigate spatial change. UCR emphasizes GIS and Earth observation.
Utrecht examines planning theories. UCR applies spatial tools to environmental problems.
Utrecht studies how places are represented in media. UCR examines race, power and representation in media.
Utrecht studies urban change through human geography and planning. UCR introduces broader social structures and inequality.
Utrecht introduces the intellectual foundations of geography and planning.
Utrecht develops theories linking migration and development across regions. UCR studies broader theories of international relations.
Utrecht studies uneven development and connections between places. UCR examines global relationships through the history of empire.
Utrecht examines debates about migration, mobility and regional development.
Utrecht applies migration research in a specialist practice lab.
Utrecht combines study of European borders with geographical fieldwork.
Utrecht develops analysis for geographical research. UCR teaches econometric methods.
Both develop empirical research design, measurement and data analysis. Utrecht applies these methods to socio-spatial questions.
Utrecht integrates methods in a project within the migration track. UCR develops qualitative research and quantitative analysis in separate courses.
Utrecht prepares students to design a geography or planning thesis.
Utrecht connects geographical research with its role in society.
Utrecht requires a 15 EC empirical thesis. The UCR comparison shows optional independent research separately.
Choose 45 EC of electives, with at least 15 EC at intermediate level or above. Options include an eligible minor, study abroad or a placement.
